concepts.title: Climate Classification by Koeppen
concepts.definition: Vladimir Koeppen classified world climates by monthly temperature and precipitation into tropical rainy A, dry B, warm temperate rainy C, cold snowy D and polar E groups with letter subtypes for rainfall seasonality and heat, giving the most widely used empirical climate scheme.
concepts.key_idea: Koeppen's capital letters denote major groups, small letters like f, w and s denote rainfall regimes and capitals like S, W, T and F refine dry and cold types.

concepts.title: Climate Change, Global Warming and Its Causes and Impacts
concepts.definition: Climate change shows in rising global temperatures of about 0.6 degrees over the century, retreating glaciers, rising sea levels and shifting rainfall belts, driven by greenhouse gases from burning fossil fuels, deforestation and land use change, alongside natural volcanic and orbital factors.
concepts.key_idea: The Kyoto Protocol and UNFCCC negotiations seek emission cuts, and the impacts threaten agriculture, sea coasts and water supplies worldwide.

concepts.title: Climate Regions of India in the World Pattern
concepts.definition: India spans several Koeppen climates from the Am tropical monsoon of the west coast, Aw savanna of the interior, BWhw hot desert of the northwest, Cwg humid subtropical of the north and the highland climates of the Himalayas, so the world climate pattern is reproduced within one country.
concepts.key_idea: This climatic variety explains India's range of crops, forests and settlement patterns from the equatorial coast to alpine heights.
